headline: WindRelay + SpyNote enable phone remote control and NFC relay for loan and card fraud
summary: A sophisticated financial fraud scheme tricks victims into installing malware, allowing attackers to remotely control phones for loans and relay NFC payments in just 13 minutes.
details: A complex financial fraud scheme leverages WindRelay and SpyNote to remotely control victim phones and relay NFC payments. Attackers can execute the entire process, from initial call to fraudulent purchase, in as little as 13 minutes.

The scheme begins with attackers posing as bank staff, tricking victims into installing a malicious SpyNote APK. This APK is customized with the victim's name and requires granting Accessibility permissions to function.

Once installed, attackers gain remote control over the device, using it to take out loans in the victim's name. They then employ WindRelay to relay real credit card NFC communication to their own device in real-time.

This NFC relay allows them to make in-store purchases at legitimate POS terminals without physically possessing the victim's card. The remote control also enables credential theft and further APK installations.

Combating this attack requires joint investigations across corporate SOCs, financial SOCs, CSIRT, and Fraud departments. Organizations must implement robust management strategies for Accessibility abuse and sideloading on Android devices.
Financial institutions are advised to prepare for correlating timelines of device risks, phone calls, loan applications, and NFC payment activities to detect and prevent such sophisticated fraud.

headline_marked: [[Claude's new AI watermarks]] spark user outrage over detection at jobs, classes
headline: Claude's new AI watermarks spark user outrage over detection at jobs, classes
summary: Anthropic's invisible code now marks Claude's editorial text as AI-generated, complying with the EU AI Act. This policy is causing significant user discontent, with many fearing exposure for using AI in professional or academic settings.
details: Anthropic has implemented a new policy to watermark Claude's outputs, embedding invisible code into the chatbot's text to identify it as AI-generated. This move is a direct response to the EU AI Act's Transparency Code, which mandates labeling of AI-generated or edited content.

While European regulators may be satisfied, many AI users are expressing strong dissatisfaction, particularly on platforms like Reddit. The primary concern among critics is the potential for these watermarks to expose their use of Claude for work or academic tasks.

One user, 'visionode,' argued that while savvy users might paraphrase to hide AI usage, the average user of Claude will be caught. They described the watermarks as a 'digital tattoo' for students or professionals who use the AI for minor assistance like reorganizing paragraphs or summarizing documents.

However, other Redditors challenged these strong reactions, pointing out that copying AI-generated summaries verbatim into articles or essays is unethical. They emphasized that the ability to detect AI-generated outputs is crucial due to the inherent risks associated with uncredited or misleading AI content.

Some critics offered more nuanced arguments, highlighting the perceived hypocrisy of an AI watermarking user-generated work when the AI itself was trained on vast amounts of other people's data. They questioned the ethical implications of an AI claiming 'credit' or asserting ownership over outputs.

Despite the backlash, many users generally support the watermarking system as a sensible method for tracking algorithmically generated material. They contend that the only reason to oppose such a system would be to intentionally misrepresent AI-generated content as original.
caption:
